summary.tagline: Explore a painter’s paradise of sea stacks, rocky islands, and rugged coastal pools.
summary.seo_title: Visiting Ballintoy Harbour | Causeway Coast Guide

travel.headline: Coastal Access at Ballintoy Harbour
travel.reservation: Access to the harbour is generally open to the public without a primary entry reservation system. Travelers should check with local Causeway Coast and Glens authorities for any temporary closures or event-based restrictions. Accommodations in the village or nearby towns should be booked independently through local providers.

days.title: Raised Beaches and Sea Stacks

stops.name: Ballintoy Harbour
stops.detail: Navigate the steep winding road to reach the picturesque harbour, sea stacks, and rocky pools. This location serves as a primary access point for exploring the 'raised beach' and cliff-top walks.

days.driving: Allow approximately 20 minutes from Ballycastle; conditions vary on the narrow access road.
days.note: The descent to the harbour is notoriously steep; use caution and maintain a slow pace.

intel.title: Steep Coastal Descent
intel.text: The harbour is reached via a spectacular, steep winding road off the B15. Drivers must be comfortable with narrow, sharp turns that lead directly to the water's edge.

intel.title: Harbour Facilities
intel.text: A car park and picnic facilities are located beside the harbour café. Space is limited, so early arrival is suggested during peak periods.

intel.title: Coastal Walking
intel.text: The site leads to significant cliff-top and beach walks. Allow several hours if planning to traverse the routes toward the wider Causeway Coast.

intel.title: Local Services
intel.text: Evidence does not specify fuel stations at the harbour; travelers should refuel in Ballycastle or Coleraine before beginning the coastal drive. Verify local availability upon arrival.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Cellular coverage in the harbour basin is not documented. It is advisable to download maps for the B15 area before descending the cliff road.

plan.arrival: Travel five miles west from Ballycastle or seventeen miles north-east of Coleraine along the B15. Identify the village of Ballintoy before turning toward the sea.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for standard cars, though the steep road may be challenging for large RVs; check rental restrictions for narrow coastal lanes.
plan.goldenHour: The sea stacks and rocky islands provide a dramatic backdrop for sunset photography, though light varies by season.
